An input .h5mu file will 
first be split in order to run the multisample processing per modality. Next, the modalities
are merged again and the integration setup pipeline is executed. Please note that this workflow
assumes that samples from multiple pipelines are already concatenated.

### Highly variable features detection

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--highly_variable_features_var_output`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
In which .var slot to store a boolean array corresponding to the highly variable genes.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"filter_with_hvg"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--highly_variable_features_obs_batch_key`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
If specified, highly-variable genes are selected within each batch separately and merged. This simple
process avoids the selection of batch-specific genes and acts as a lightweight batch correction method.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"sample_id"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--highly_variable_features_features_to_exclude`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
User-defined list of feature names to exclude from HVG calculation. These features will be excluded from HVG selection but will remain in the output data.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"MT-CO1"`, `"MT-CO2"`, `"MT-ND1"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::::

### QC metrics calculation options

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--var_qc_metrics`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Keys to select a boolean (containing only True or False) column from .var.
For each cell, calculate the proportion of total values for genes which are labeled 'True',
compared to the total sum of the values for all genes.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"filter_with_hvg"`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"ercc,highly_variable"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `","`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--top_n_vars`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Number of top vars to be used to calculate cumulative proportions.
If not specified, proportions are not calculated. `--top_n_vars 20,50` finds
cumulative proportion to the 20th and 50th most expressed vars.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `50`, `100`, `200`, `500`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `","`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--log1p_transform`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Compute log1p-transformed versions of the calculated QC metrics. For each emitted
metric column `<col>`, an additional column `log1p_<col>` is added containing
`log1p(<col>)`. Mirrors scanpy's `log1p` flag.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean`

[Default]{.arg-key} `true`
:::
::::
:::::

### RNA Scaling options

Options for enabling scaling of the log-normalized data to unit variance and zero mean.
The scaled data will be output a different layer and representation with reduced dimensions
will be created and stored in addition to the non-scaled data.

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--rna_enable_scaling`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Enable scaling for the RNA modality.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean_true`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--rna_scaling_output_layer`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Output layer where the scaled log-normalized data will be stored.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"scaled"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--rna_scaling_pca_obsm_output`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Name of the .obsm key where the PCA representation of the log-normalized
and scaled data is stored.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"scaled_pca"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--rna_scaling_pca_loadings_varm_output`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Name of the .varm key where the PCA loadings of the log-normalized and scaled
data is stored.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"scaled_pca_loadings"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--rna_scaling_pca_variance_uns_output`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Name of the .uns key where the variance and variance ratio will be stored as a map.
The map will contain two keys: variance and variance_ratio respectively.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"scaled_pca_variance"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--rna_scaling_umap_obsm_output`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Name of the .obsm key where the UMAP representation of the log-normalized and scaled data is stored.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"scaled_umap"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--rna_scaling_max_value`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Clip (truncate) data to this value after scaling. If not specified, do not clip.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--rna_scaling_zero_center`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
If set, omit zero-centering variables, which allows to handle sparse input efficiently."
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean_false`
:::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/multiomics/process_batches/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/workflows/multiomics/process_batches);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/multiomics/process_batches/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
